introduction: Just as Panchayati Raj deals with rural areas, Municipalities deal with the local self-government of urban areas (cities and towns). The system ensures that urban development, sanitation, and local issues are managed by the people's elected representatives rather than central or state authorities.

core_concepts.title: 74th Constitutional Amendment Act (1992)
core_concepts.description: This act gave constitutional status to the municipalities. It added a new Part IX-A to the Constitution and a new 12th Schedule.

core_concepts.title: Three Types of Municipalities
core_concepts.description: 1. Nagar Panchayat (for a transitional area, i.e., an area changing from rural to urban). 2. Municipal Council (for a smaller urban area). 3. Municipal Corporation (for a larger urban area, like big cities).

core_concepts.title: Composition and Terms
core_concepts.description: All members of a municipality are elected directly by the people. The municipal area is divided into territorial constituencies called 'Wards'. The term of office is 5 years. The minimum age to contest elections is 21 years.

core_concepts.title: First Municipal Corporation
core_concepts.description: The first municipal corporation in India was set up in Madras (Chennai) in 1687-88, followed by Bombay and Calcutta in 1726.

important_entities.name: Lord Ripon
important_entities.key_fact: Father of Local Self-Government in India
important_entities.significance: His resolution of 1882 is hailed as the 'Magna Carta' of local self-government, as it laid the foundation for democratic municipal governance under British rule.

important_entities.name: The Mayor
important_entities.significance: The Mayor is the ceremonial head of the municipal corporation, while the real administrative power lies with the Municipal Commissioner (usually an IAS officer).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Do not confuse the two. A 'Gram Panchayat' is strictly for a rural village. A 'Nagar Panchayat' is for an area that is currently transitioning from a village into a town (semi-urban).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Panchayats = 73rd Amendment, 11th Schedule. Municipalities = 74th Amendment, 12th Schedule. They usually go hand-in-hand.

exam_strategy_tips: Always remember the minimum age for municipal elections is 21 years (not 18, not 25).
Questions regarding the first Municipal Corporation (Madras, 1687) are very common in basic competitive exams.
